headline: Profit climbs on rate recoveries, guidance held steady
summary_short: Duke Energy's Q2 FY2026 GAAP EPS rose 10.4% y/y to $1.38 (adjusted EPS $1.43, +14.4% y/y) as revenue grew 3.0% y/y to $7,592M; the company reaffirmed its FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.55-$6.80.
summary_long: Revenue rose 3.0% y/y to $7,592M and net income grew 11.0% y/y to $1,092M ($1.38 GAAP EPS, +10.4% y/y). Adjusted EPS of $1.43 (+14.4% y/y) excludes a $0.05/share charge from Duke Energy Carolinas' North Carolina rate-case settlement. Electric Utilities segment income rose to $1,271M ($1,310M adjusted) as recovery of infrastructure investment (+$0.15/share) was partly offset by higher depreciation and interest expense on a growing asset base. Gas Utilities income was flat at $10M as infrastructure-investment recovery was offset by lower earnings following the sale of Piedmont's Tennessee gas business. Cash rose to $673M from $245M at year-end; long-term debt grew to $82,242M from $80,108M. Duke reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.55-$6.80 and its 5-7% long-term growth rate through 2030.

drivers.explanation: Growth came from continuing rider and rate-case increases across the Carolinas, Florida, Ohio and Indiana jurisdictions plus higher wholesale sales; retail electric volumes were roughly flat y/y.

Higher adjusted results came from infrastructure-investment recovery in growing service territories, partly offset by higher depreciation and interest expense on a larger asset base; reported EPS also absorbed a $0.05/share North Carolina rate-case settlement charge.
Operating income growth reflects the same drivers cited for EPS and segment income - infrastructure-investment recovery and rate-case increases outpacing higher depreciation, O&M and interest costs.

Net income growth tracks EPS: infrastructure-investment recovery and constructive rate-case outcomes lifted results, partly offset by the North Carolina settlement charge and higher depreciation/interest expense on a growing asset base.

CEO Harry Sideris cited a strong first half with constructive regulatory outcomes and advancing strategic priorities, positioning the company to deliver on 2026 commitments and pursue growth in its service states.
